title: The SSF conformance PR added GET/PATCH/PUT stream handlers plus stream verify and status views without the add_stream provider permission check that the existing POST handler enforces, so any token holder for the app can read, modify, verify and disable its event streams.

findings.explanation: All database interactions use Django ORM fields and model definitions; no raw SQL strings or string‑concatenated queries are introduced.

evidence.content:
class Stream(models.Model):
    uuid = models.UUIDField(default=uuid4, primary_key=True, editable=False)
    status = models.TextField(choices=StreamStatus.choices, default=StreamStatus.ENABLED)
    provider = models.ForeignKey(SSFProvider, on_delete=models.CASCADE)
    delivery_method = models.TextField(choices=DeliveryMethods.choices)
    endpoint_url = models.TextField(null=True)
    authorization_header = models.TextField(null=True, default=None)
    events_requested = ArrayField(models.TextField(choices=EventTypes.choices), default=list)
    format = models.TextField()

findings.explanation: The SSFStreamViewSet exposes Retrieve, Destroy, and List actions on the full Stream queryset (Stream.objects.all()) without any ownership or permission checks, allowing a user to access or delete streams they do not own (potential IDOR).

evidence.content:
class SSFStreamViewSet(
    mixins.RetrieveModelMixin,
    mixins.DestroyModelMixin,
    mixins.ListModelMixin,
    GenericViewSet,
):
    """SSFStream Viewset"""

    queryset = Stream.objects.all()

findings.suggested_fix: Add appropriate permission classes (e.g., IsAuthenticated & custom object‑level permission) and filter the queryset to only include streams owned by the requesting user or associated provider, e.g., `queryset = Stream.objects.filter(provider__owner=request.user)` or override `get_queryset` to enforce ownership.
